author: bunderwood
title: Cobb diner gets failing health score after 14 violations - NewsBreak
text:
By bunderwood ,
1 days ago West Cobb Diner is shown. By Bo Underwood | bunderwood@mdjonline.com MARIETTA — A Cobb County diner received a failing health score after an inspector found 14 violations, including handwashing, food storage and temperature violations.
West Cobb Diner, located at 3451 Barrett Parkway, received a 55 out of 100 during Tuesday’s routine health inspection.
“I definitely, obviously, want to apologize,” general manager Tim Huddleston told the MDJ. ‘“It’s definitely not our standard. We look forward to serving all of our customers, and we have much, much higher standards than that. Ultimately, it was just a few things.”
Health inspections are conducted by the Georgia Department of Public Health. The score is categorized under the letter grade “U” for unsatisfactory compliance with the health code.
There are four letter grades a restaurant can receive during an inspection: an “A” for scores between 90 and 100, a “B” for scores between 80 and 89, a “C” for scores between 70 and 79 and a “U” for an overall score of 69 or lower, according to the Georgia Department of Public Health.
The diner previously scored a 91 this January and an 89 in October 2024.
The diner’s 14 violations included improper handwashing procedures, raw food being exposed to cross-contamination, improper use of time as a health control and heavy black and green slime on the ice machine lid in the main kitchen. All violations were corrected on-site.
According to the report, employees were observed washing their hands for less than 10 seconds and turning off the faucet with their bare hands rather than using paper towels. A hand sink was observed without any hand soap or hand drying provisions.
Several foods throughout the kitchen were left uncovered, including trout butter, gravy, pickles, corndogs, onions and olives.
Two containers of buttermilk were observed next to a fryer with no label for when they needed to be thrown away. Several unlabeled squirt bottles throughout the main kitchen were observed throughout the main kitchen.
Additional violations included a large amount of food debris found on the floor of the walk-in cooler and throughout the main kitchen, raw chicken stored above raw uncovered pork and a Certified Food Protection Manager certificate displayed for a manager that is no longer with the company.
Temperature violations included several foods being stored above the required 41 degrees, food not cooled at a fast enough rate and foods being stored below the required 135 degrees. All affected food was discarded.
“We're doing some more stuff today,” Huddleston said. “Making sure everybody’s doing some more training, making sure everybody knows what needs to be held at what temp. Making sure the thing's labeled correctly. Washing the hands properly.
“So we're looking forward to our next health inspection, which should be in a few days, and we’re looking forward to an A.”
